text:
Alice: Quick idea — propose a hybrid deploy-time warmer that uses autoscaler hooks + short scheduled jobs to prefill KV for the new model shard on deploy. Goals: hit-rate spike during rollout, minimal extra GPU cycles, and avoid thrashing kernel selection. Thoughts?
Ben: +1 on autoscaler hooks. We saw regressions when warmers flood the device and the runtime flips to a generic kernel path.
Ben: profiling snapshot: 
```
seq_len=64 batch=16 kernel=matmul_opt_v1 t=12.3ms
seq_len=64 batch=128 kernel=matmul_generic t=45.8ms   # when lots of warmers run
KV_serving_threads=32 cpu_util=94%
```
Carol: That kernel flip is the crux — warmers should avoid creating large concurrent batches that change the kernel selection heuristic. Suggest: warmers should emit variable seq lengths and a spread-out temporal pattern so the scheduler keeps the optimized kernels.
Dave: +1. Also think about key normalization: our current warmers use full prompt text as cache keys. That creates too many unique keys and low hit amplification. We should canonicalize prefixes to the first N tokens + metadata hash.
Erin: Example normalization we ran locally: `prefix_key = sha256(prefix[:64] + role_tag)[:16]` — hit-rate went from 12% -> 28% on dev traces.
Alice: Nice. Can we combine both? Warmers that (1) schedule via autoscaler prelaunch window, (2) use canonicalized keys, (3) limit concurrent batch size to <32, and (4) include short tail interleaving so kernel heuristics stay on optimized path.
Ben: There is also an interaction with eviction TTL. If warmers run too early, evictions during the deploy push keys out before traffic arrives. Maybe tie warmers to rollout phases: preseed -> continuous trickle -> on-demand top-up.
Carol: Agree. Proposed phases: 
- preseed: run once at deploy with canonical keys, low concurrency
- trickle: scheduled job every 30s for 10m to keep hotsets
- top-up: autoscaler hook when new instance spins up for immediate fill
Dave: Sounds good. Concern: synthetic warmers produce different KV key distributions than real traffic. We should capture a small sample of production prompts and derive canonical prefixes from that for fidelity.
Erin: I ran a 1h prober against canary with `./prober --sample prod-prefixes.json --rate 5rps` — link to perf graph: https://internal.perf/graphs/2546 (works only internally). Observed: preseed + trickle gave 3x higher 1s hit-rate and 18% lower p99 latency for small seq workloads.
deploy-bot: deploy/infra 2546004321 started by Alice — canary 3/3 healthy :rocket:
Ben: One more gotcha — kernel selection uses a moving window of recent batch sizes. If warmers interleave but push average batch size up, the runtime still picks the slower kernel. We need a warmers flag so the runtime treats those requests as "priming" and excludes them from kernel selection metrics.
Carol: If engine-level change is hard, a workaround: warmers should intentionally emit a small fraction of larger batches that mimic production batch distribution but keep overall avg below threshold. Ugly but doable.
Alice: Action items: 
- Dave: implement prefix canonicalization + sample-based prefix extractor (ETA 2d)
- Erin: run 24h canary with preseed+trickle config and collect kernel selection traces (ETA 3d)
- Ben: prototype a warmers runtime flag to mark requests as priming (spike-protection) and measure impact (ETA 1w)
- Carol: draft rollout plan with phases and eviction TTL tuning (ETA 2d)
Dave: will add a small CLI option `--canonicalize-prefix --sample-size=1000` to the prober.
Erin: I'll add a perf dashboard tile for kernel selection transitions and KV hit-rate by phase.
Alice: Sweet. If no objections I’ll open a RFC PR with this plan and the perf data once Erin finishes the canary. :thumbsup:
Ben: go for it.
Carol: lgtm
Dave: lgtm
Erin: lgtm
Alice: thanks all!
